record.context_brief: elastic G-closure with void or rigid phase
record.original_question: Take a composite formed by mixing an isotropic elastic phase with either a void phase or a rigid phase. Can one completely characterize the resulting G-closure, that is, the full set of effective elasticity tensors obtainable from all such microstructures?

evidence.quote: Problem 8: Can one complete the characterization of the G-closure for a void (or rigid) phase mixed with an isotropic elastic phase?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two-phase composite materials in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) made by mixing an isotropic linearly elastic phase, with given Lamé moduli (bulk modulus $\kappa>0$ and shear modulus $\mu>0$), with a second phase that is either void (zero stiffness) or rigid (infinite stiffness). For a given volume fraction $\theta\in(0,1)$ of the elastic phase, consider all possible periodic (or, equivalently, all measurable) microstructures and form the set of effective elasticity tensors $C^*$ obtained by homogenization, where $C^*$ is a positive (semi)definite, fully symmetric fourth-order tensor relating average strain to average stress. The G-closure $\mathcal{G}_\theta$ is defined as the closure (in the appropriate $H$-convergence topology) of the set of all such effective tensors realizable as some microstructure varies.

Problem: Provide a complete characterization of the G-closure $\mathcal{G}_\theta$ for the elastic+void mixture, and likewise for the elastic+rigid mixture. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a fourth-order tensor $C^*$ for it to belong to $\mathcal{G}_\theta$, for every volume fraction $\theta\in(0,1)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The weak G-closure (sharp bounds on coexistent stress-strain pairs and on effective compliance/energy) is known: Allaire–Kohn (rigid+elastic) and Gibiansky–Cherkaev/Allaire (void+elastic) provided sharp energy bounds and identified extremal microstructures (near-optimal unimodes and pentamodes). However, the full G-closure—a complete characterization of all attainable effective elasticity tensors—remains unresolved in general, particularly in 3D.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems in Elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Lists complete G-closure characterization for elastic composites among long-standing open problems in elasticity.
status_evidence.claim: The full G-closure for elastic mixtures is listed as an open problem in elasticity.

status_evidence.title: Sharp bounds and pentamode/unimode extremal microstructures
status_evidence.snippet: Allaire–Kohn and Gibiansky–Cherkaev/Allaire solved the weak G-closure problem for elastic+rigid and elastic+void composites via sharp energy bounds, with extremals being near-optimal unimodes and pentamodes.
status_evidence.claim: Weak G-closure is solved in both cases, but full G-closure characterization remains incomplete.
